title: Operator Sprintbox: Autotaskify legacy admin utilities
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We have ~30 legacy admin utilities (shell scripts, Ad-Hoc Playbooks, and 2 small Flask apps) used by SRE and Support that are brittle, undocumented, and hard to audit. They are not represented as runnable task objects in Linear / the Runbook runtime which prevents dry-run, RBAC gating, and unified telemetry.

Goal: Convert the highest-value utilities into first-class runbook tasks that can be executed via the new Operator Sprintbox UI/CLI, support dry-run & replay, include idempotency checks, enforce RBAC & approval flows, and emit structured telemetry compatible with Console tracing and billing attribution. This ticket drives the initial conversion and instrumentation for the first 7 utilities (account reset, instance drain, log-archive, certificate-refresh, quota-reconcile, tracing-collector-attach, and compact-db-snapshot).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each converted utility is stored as a runbook-as-task manifest with typed inputs in the runbook registry; 2) Sprintbox can surface the tasks by tag and present 'Dry Run' and 'Execute' modes; 3) Tasks enforce idempotency tokens and record execution provenance to the ops-telemetry topic; 4) RBAC gate + optional 2nd approver flow works for P0/P1 actions; 5) End-to-end test harness (playback with synthetic data) validates no side-effects in dry-run and correct side-effects in execute mode; 6) Observability: per-execution traces appear in Console under runbook-executions and include cost & latency breakdown; 7) First tranche of 7 utilities converted and verified in staging with documented runbook manifests and PRs linked.
comments: 2025-03-05 - Maya Chen: Created ticket and initial scoping doc. Prioritized set of 7 utilities with SRE lead input.

2025-03-06 - Arjun Patel: Spike completed for converting 'account reset' into runbook manifest. Found that existing script assumes direct DB access; added adapter layer to go through admin-api. Decision: always prefer service adapters over direct DB changes to preserve audit trail.
2025-03-08 - Review (Liam O'Conner): UX comment - include 'estimated cost' shown before execution. Engineering follow-up: add token-estimator to Sprintbox surface (low-pri enhancement if time).

2025-03-09 - Security review: flagged certificate-refresh for additional KMS validation. Security required a short threat model and confirmed HSM usage for private keys. Marking security_review_required for that subtask.

2025-03-10 - Arjun Patel: Implemented dry-run shim and idempotency token generation. Dry-run returns an execution-plan JSON and emits a trace without side-effects. Added unit tests for idempotency wrappers.
2025-03-12 - Maya Chen: Integration test against staging runbook-registry passed for first 4 utilities. Next: complete remaining 3 and polish telemetry schema to include cost attribution fields.

Notes: Keep conversions small and reversible. Where possible, wrap legacy scripts instead of rewriting to reduce blast radius. All conversions must include a plain-English playbook doc in Drive for oncall reference.
